result.question: How is NITI Aayog different from the erstwhile Planning Commission? Evaluate its role in promoting cooperative federalism. (Answer in 150 words)

directives.meaning: Weigh the merits and limits and give a clear judgement on how well it works.

sentences.text: The Planning Commission, set up in 1950 with the Prime Minister as its Chairperson, was replaced in January 2015 by NITI Aayog, the National Institution for Transforming India.
The Planning Commission followed a largely top-down approach, whereas NITI Aayog is designed as a think tank that favours bottom-up planning.
The Planning Commission allocated plan funds to states, but NITI Aayog has no power to allocate funds.
Its Governing Council includes the Chief Ministers of all states and of union territories with legislatures, along with the Lieutenant Governors of other union territories.
Regional councils, convened by the Prime Minister, address issues affecting more than one state.
It encourages competitive federalism by ranking states on indices such as the SDG India Index.
It also offers states policy advice and capacity-building support, acting as their partner at the Centre.
However, because it controls no funds, its influence over state priorities depends largely on persuasion.
Stronger state-level think tanks can make NITI Aayog an effective engine of Team India.
